transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let me first give you a sports update.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The Braves, one; the Cardinals, nothing, early on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want to thank you and I want to thank everybody here tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I want to give a special thanks to my wife Elizabeth, my daughter Robin for their love and support, and thank the people who are listening and watching all over America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In 20 days, you will help decide who will lead this country into the next century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s an awesome responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And you must ask yourself, do you know enough about the candidates?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You should know as much as possible about each of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes the views have been distorted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There’s been millions and millions of dollars of negative advertising spent distorting my views.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I hope tonight you will get a better feel of who Bob Dole is and what he’s all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think first you should — I should understand that the question on your mind is do I understand your problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Would I understand it if it occurred to me, and I might just say I’m from a large family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I got lots of relatives and they’re good, average, middle-class, hardworking Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They live all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re not all Republicans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Maybe all but one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But in any event, I understand the problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Whether it’s two parents working because one has to pay the taxes and one has to provide for the family, whether it’s a single parent who just barely pays the pressing bills or whether you’re worried about an education for your children going to the best schools, or whether you’re worried about safe playgrounds, drug-free schools, crime-free schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is what this election is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And hopefully tonight when we conclude this debate you will have a better understanding and the viewing and listening audience will have a better understanding.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I was going to applaud, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And thanks to the people of San Diego for giving us this opportunity to have another discussion about the decision we all face in front of people who will make the decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Again, I will say I will do my best to make this a discussion of ideas and issues, not insults.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What really matters is what happens to your future and what happens to our country as we stand on the brink of a new century, a time of extraordinary possibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have a simple philosophy that I tried to follow for the last four years: Do what creates opportunity for all, what reinforces responsibility from all of us, and what will help us build a community where everybody’s got a role to play and a place at the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Compared to four years ago, we’re clearly better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got ten and a half million more jobs, the deficit’s been reduced by 60 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Incomes are rising for the first time in a decade, the crime rates, the welfare rolls are falling, we’re putting , 100,000 more police on the street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 60,000 felons, fugitives and stalkers have been denied handguns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But that progress is only the beginning.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What we really should focus on tonight is what we still have to do to help the American people make the most of this future that’s out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think what really matters is what we can do to build strong families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Strong families need a strong economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: To me that means we have to go on and balance this budget while we protect Medicare and Medicaid and education and the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We should give a tax cut, targeted to child rearing and education, to buying a first home and paying for health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We ought to help protect our kids from drugs and guns and gangs and tobacco.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We ought to help move a million people from welfare to work and we ought to create the finest education system in the world where every 18-year-old can go on to college and all of our younger children have great educational opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If we do those things, we can build that bridge to the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I hope to get to talk about tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Hi.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: MS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: McAFEE: My name is Shannon McAfee.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m a beginning educator in this country, and I really think it’s important what children have to say.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re still very idealistic.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And they — everything they say comes from the heart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I have a quote for you from “If I Were President,” compiled by Peggy Gavin.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: A sixth grader says, “If I were president, I would think about Abraham Lincoln and George Washington and what they did to make our country great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We should unite the white and black people and people of all cultures.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Democrats and Republicans should unite also.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We should all come together and think of the best ways to solve the economic problems of our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: “I believe that when we are able to come together and stop fighting amongst ourselves we will get along a lot better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: ” These are the ideals and morals that we are teach — we are trying to teach our children in these days.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Yet we don’t seem to be practicing them in our government, in anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If you are president, how will you begin to practice what we are preaching to our children, the future of our nation?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I would say first of all, I think, it’s a very good question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I appreciate the quote from the young man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt about it that many American people have lost their faith in government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They see scandals almost on a daily basis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They see ethical problems in the Whitehouse today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They see 900 FBI files, private person, being gathered up by somebody in the Whitehouse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Nobody knows who hired this man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So there’s a great deal of cynicism out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I’ve always tried in whatever I’ve done is to bring people together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I said in my acceptance speech in San Diego about two months ago that the exits are clearly marked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If you think the Republican party is some place for you to come if you’re narrow minded or bigoted or don’t like certain people in America, the exits are clearly marked for you to walk out of as I stand here without compromise, because this is the party of Lincoln.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think we have a real obligation, obviously public officials.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m no longer a public official.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I left public life on June the 11th of this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But it is very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Young people are looking to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re looking to us for leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re watching what we do, what we say, what we promise and what we finally deliver.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I would think, it seems to me that there are opportunities here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When I’m President of the United States, I will keep my word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: My word is my bond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons that I ran for president, Sandy, is because not just children, a lot of grownups felt that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And if you remember four years ago, we had not only rising unemployment, but a lot of rising cynicism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I had never worked in Washington as an elected official.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It seemed to me that most of the arguments were partisan, Republican, Democrat, left, right, liberal, conservative.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I said tonight I’m for opportunity, responsibility and community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve gotten some real progress in the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve also done everything I could at every moment of division in this country, after Oklahoma City, when these churches were burned, to bring people together and remind people that we are stronger because of our diversity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to respect one another.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You mentioned Washington and Lincoln.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They were presidents at historic times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is an historic time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s important we go beyond those old partisan arguments and focus on people and their future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When we do that, instead of shutting the government down over a partisan fight over the budget, we’re a better country and that’s why we’re making progress now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, bringing people together, again, is obviously a responsibility we all have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know you do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Everybody here does it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You do a lot of things nobody knows about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I have a little foundation for the disabled called the Dole Foundation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve raised about $10 million.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We don’t talk about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We try to help people with disabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Bring them back into the mainstream of public life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So it seems to me that there’s also a public trust.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When you’re the president of the United States, you have a public trust and you have to keep that public trust, as George Washington, as Abraham Lincoln did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think now that trust is being violated and it seems to me we ought to face up to it, and the president ought to say tonight that he’s not going to pardon anybody that he was involved in business with who might implicate him later on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I will.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, let me say what we have done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In the last four years we’ve worked hard to promote more competition to bring down the rate of inflation in health care costs without eroding health care quality.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The government pays for Medicare and Medicaid, as you know, and that’s very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we’ve added a million more children to the ranks of the insured through the Medicaid program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have protected 25 million people through the passage of the Kennedy-Kassebaum bill that says you can use your health insurance if you change jobs or someone in your family has been sick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We just recently ended those drive-by deliveries saying people can’t be kicked out of the hospital by insurance companies when they’ve just had babies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So this is, that’s a good start.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In the next four years, I want to focus on the following things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number one, add another million children to the insured ranks through the Medicaid program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number two, keep working with the states, as we are now, to add 2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 2 million more people to the insurance system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number three, cover people who are between jobs for up to six months.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That could protect 3 million families, 700,000 kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Number four, make sure we protect the integrity with the Medicare program and Medicaid program and not do anything in cutting costs which would cause hundreds of hospitals to close which could have been the case if the 270billion dollar Medicare cut that I vetoed, had been enacted in the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, first, let me say there you go again, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, talking about a Medicare cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I have heard you say this time after time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I have heard you say on one TV appearance, “the media made me do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: ” You were trying to defend your cut which was not a cut either, Reduction in the growth of spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve always had at least 7 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’ve said publicly that it’s now three times the rate of inflation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to cut the growth to twice the rate of inflation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s about where we are now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So let’s stop talking about cutting Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In my economic plan we increase it 39percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Don’t forget what he tried to do with health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 17 new taxes, spend 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 5 trillion dollars, 50 new bureaucracies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Can you believe that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You couldn’t even have been a cardiologist because he had quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re a cardiologist, it wouldn’t affect you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But if somebody wanted to be a cardiologist, ten years from now, you’d have to be certain you complied with some of the rules in this extreme medical plan the government was going to take over for all Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are things we can do like the Kassebaum bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We changed many provisions I authored, cover preexisting conditions, portability, and there are other things we can do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We still need to cover about 20million people and a lot of children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have time in 30 seconds to respond to fix all that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But let me just say the American Hospital Association said that the budget I vetoed could have closed 700 hospitals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Not me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: On a per-person basis, it did cut way below the rate of inflation in medical costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the important thing is what are we going to do now?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to help people who are between jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to cover more kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Provide more preventative care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My balanced budget covers mammograms for ladies, women on Medicare and also gives respite care to the million-plus families who have someone with Alzheimerâ€™s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: These things are paid for in the balanced budget plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’ll move us forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Jason, I appreciate that very much, being a former military man myself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, we have 17,000 men and women today wearing our uniform that receive food stamps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It shouldn’t happen in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have men and women wearing our uniform in substandard housing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It shouldn’t happen in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it’s time we take a look at the pay scales.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Did get a 3 percent increase this year, but that’s not enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If we’re going to ask young men and young women to protect us and defend us around the world, and we’ve had more deployments under this administration than any time in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Fifty times we deployed troops around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Every time you do that you take a risk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Somebody, you know, maybe your son, maybe your grandson, maybe somebody else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I think anybody who wears a uniform is a great American.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Remember Vietnam?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Remember when people almost used to walk across the street rather than have a contact with somebody who was in Vietnam?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s all behind us now, and it should be behind us, and the forgotten war, the Korean War, but I guess I can just answer you very plainly, Jason.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you for doing what you’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: America owes you a debt of gratitude.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: May I ask you a question?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What service are you in?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And what kind of small business do you have?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Good for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say, if Senator Dole mentioned this, I just signed a bill that we got through Congress to increase the amount of pay increase we could give for military personnel and to make sure the pay increase this year was above the rate of inflation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I also presented to the Congress and they adopted a large package of quality-of-life improvements, which are very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I spent a lot of time talking to military families as well as military members all over the world and in bases all across the United States, and I became convinced after talking to the families and the personnel in uniform that we needed to not only have the pay raise but we needed to invest more in child care, housing, and other things to support families, especially when there are longer deployments because of the downsizing of the military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I, we’re going to do better, and we’ll do better still, but this is a commitment I think that all Americans share without regard to party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t disagree with anything that the President said, except he waited four years to do these things, and my view is it ought to be, it will be done on Day 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ll start working on Day 1 in the Dole- Kemp administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We only have ten divisions now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We used to have 18.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had 25 fighter wings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re down to 13.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had 536 ships.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re down to 336 ships.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I mean, we’ve cut defense spending too much in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President told you in ’92 he would cut it 67 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He cut 112 billion dollars, so we’re right on the edge right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But the last thing we ought to do is make those who wear the uniforms sacrifice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me just take two seconds of my time because I’m the Commander-in-Chief to respond to one thing that was said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I propose to spend 1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: 6 trillion dollars on defense between now and the year 2002 and there’s less than 1 percent difference between my budget and the Republican budget on defense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, on the Middle East, as you know, I worked very hard for peace in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The agreement between the Palestinians and the Israelis was signed at the White House and the agreement — the peace treaty with Jordan, I was — I went to Jordan to sign that — to be there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But — and I think the United States can do whatever we reasonably can.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I can say this: I do not believe Yassir Arafat wants us to send troops to the West Bank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have never been asked to send troops to the West Bank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I saw the agreement that Prime Minister Rabin and Yassir Arafat signed on the West Bank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It had 26 separate maps they had to sign, literally thousands of delineations of who would do what on the West Bank, and I believe if the parties will get together and in a good-faith manner make that agreement, that they’ll be able to do it if we cannot impose a peace on the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My position has always been that the job of the United States was to minimize the risks of peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, if they asked me to be part of some monitoring force — as we are in the Sinai and have been since 1978 — to monitor the peace between Egypt and Israel, frankly, I would have to think about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would have to see what they wanted to do, but I don’t believe that will be the request.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think what Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Arafat wants us to do is to make sure that everybody honors the agreements they’ve already made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I brought the leaders to Washington a few days ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think they will, and I think we’ll get there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Don’t be too discouraged.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let me, Jason, come back to you a minute because there is a big difference in the defense budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had 7 billion this year and 10 billion more than the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He puts his money in the outyears, and even if he were re-elected, he’d be gone before anything would happen, and nothing is going to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We don’t have modernization now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If we don’t build more B-2 bombers in California and we lost about 500,000 jobs out in California, because of this devastation, these big, big cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had to make cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t have the cuts the president promised he’d make and then he doubled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to go back and take a look.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re increasing defense reasonably — not too much, but we are increasing defense some — because we want to be prepared in case somebody here gets called up, Jason.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I would say I didn’t hear what Yassir Arafat had to say, but I don’t want to — you know, I think foreign policy, I want to be very careful about, and I’m not here to argue about the President with some ongoing foreign policy matter.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: What I want the President to do, and I think he may have done it, his last statement, call for an unconditional end of the violence and have the parties keep on talking as they should talk and have a resolution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The last thing we want to do is commit more forces anywhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But let’s sort of keep this out of politics because it’s pretty dicey right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When the change of government occurred in Israel, the people of Israel were saying we don’t want to abandon the peace process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We want more security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then a lot of mutual distrust developed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A lot of things happened which maybe shouldn’t have happened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I asked Yassir Arafat and Prime Minister Netanyahu to come to Washington and got them together and they talked alone for three hours, I was convinced that they had to have a chance to make that peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Again, I’d say if they asked us to play some reasonable role, I don’t know how I would respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It would depend entirely on what they asked us to do, but the real secret there is for them to abide by the agreements they’ve made and find a way to trust each other, and they’re going to have to spend some time and trust each other.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Prime Minister Rabin gave his life believing that that trust could be materialized, and I still think it can be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Oh, that’s very easy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: My record going back to 1965 in the Congress, the first vote we had was whether or not you should put a little notice on cigarettes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They may be danger — I voted I for everything since that time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In fact, 1992 we had a bill come before us that all the states had to comply or they’re going to lose certain money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We sent it to the Clinton Administration for implementation, and they waited three and a half years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And during that period about 3,000 young kids every day started smoking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So you add it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s about three million.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Not until again in 1996 — I don’t want anybody to smoke.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: My brother probably died partly because of cigarettes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I was asked a technical question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Are they addictive?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Maybe they — they probably are addictive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m not a doctor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You shouldn’t smoke.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You ought to be glad you quit, Oscar, 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it seems to me what we need to do is to talk about not only tobacco but drugs, because drug use between 12- and 17-year-olds has doubled in this administration in the last 44 months.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Marijuana use is up 141percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Cocaine use up 160 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re your kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s all happening in this administration because they cut funding and they cut interdiction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When I’m President of the United States, we’re going to use the National Guard and whatever sources we need to stop some of the drugs coming into America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If you stop the drugs, nobody is going to use the drugs; so don’t smoke, don’t drink, don’t use drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Just don’t do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Oscar, the question of what the federal government should do to limit the access of tobacco to young people is one of the biggest differences between Senator Dole and me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We did propose a regulation six months after I became President under the law he mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It simply says all these states — it made it illegal for kids to smoke.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now they have to try harder if they want to keep getting federal funds.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then we took comments, as we always do, and there were tens of thousands of comments as to how we ought to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s what drug it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Meanwhile, we started the — also in ’93 to look into whether cigarettes were addictive enough for the Federal Food and Drug Administration to ban the ability of cigarette companies to advertise, market and distribute their products to our kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No president had ever taken on the tobacco lobby before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole opposed me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He went down and made a speech to people who were on his side saying that I did the wrong thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think I did the right thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: On drugs, I have repeatedly said drugs are wrong and illegal and can kill you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have strengthened enforcement, and everybody in San Diego knows we strengthened control of the border.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have done a lot more, and I hope we get a chance to talk about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, they also know if they live in San Diego, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, if you’re caught with 125 pounds of marijuana or less, you go back to Mexico.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re not prosecuted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You have a U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: attorney here that sends `em back home, so I think that’s pretty important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s a lot of marijuana.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s a big supply.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But don’t get into this smoke screen here Oscar.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President in the election year decided I ought to do something, I haven’t done anything on drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been AWOL for 44 months, so let’s take on smoking, see they haven’t even done it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They haven’t said what’s going to happen, whether they’re going to have it declared addictive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Once it’s a drug, does it apply only to teenagers or everybody in America?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Nobody should smoke, young or old, but particularly young people should not smoke, but my record is there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s been there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’ve voted eight, ten times since 1965.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, there are two different things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Social Security and Medicare are entirely different in terms of the financial stabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about them separately.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Social Security is stable until, as you pointed out, at least the third decade of the next century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we’d like to have a Social Security fund that has about 70 years of life instead of about 30 years of life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: What we have to do is simply to make some adjustments to take account of the fact that the baby boomers, people like me, are bigger in number than the people that went just before us and the people that come just after us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I think what we’ll plainly do is what we did in 1983 when Senator Dole served, and this is something I think he did a good job on when he served on the Social Security commission and they made some modest changes in Social Security to make sure that it would be alive and well into the 21st century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we will do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s obvious that there are certain things that have to be done and there are 50 or 60 different options, and a bipartisan commission to take it out of politics, will make recommendations and build support for the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Medicare is different.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Medicare needs help now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have proposed a budget which would put ten years on the life of the Medicare trust fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s more than it’s had a lot of the time in the last years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It would save a lot of money through more managed care, by giving more options, more preventative care and lowering the inflation rate and the prices we’re paying providers without having the kind of big premium increases and out-of-pocket costs that the budget I vetoed would provide.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Then that would give us ten years to do with Medicare what we’re going to do with Social Security; have a bipartisan group look at what we have to do to save it when the baby boomers retire.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But now we can, we ought to pass this budget now and put ten years on it right away so no one has to worry about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well again, if you’re somebody thinking about the future, I think it’s fair to say that it’ll be — we’ll work it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is a political year, and the President is playing politics with Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: After this year is over, we’ll resolve it just as we did with Social Security in `83.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a nonpartisan commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Ronald Reagan got together with Tip O’Neill and Howard Baker, two Republicans and one Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They appointed a commission I was on that commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We resolved, we rescued Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We suggested — I think it has been over a year ago now — we do the same with Medicare, and the White House called it a gimmick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now last week I guess it was Donna Shalala said well we’ll cut Medicare a hundred billion and appoint a commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It will probably have to be done by a commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Take it out of politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think if I were a senior citizen I would be a little fed up with all these ads scaring seniors, scaring veterans and scaring students about education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When you don’t have any ideas, you don’t have any agenda, and all you have is fear, that’s all you can use.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have ideas in the Dole-Kemp campaign and we will rescue Medicare as we did Social Security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Their idea was to have the poorest seniors in the country pay $270 more this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Their idea was a budget that the that the American Hospital Association said could close 700 hospitals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Their idea was to charge everybody more out-of-pocket costs in their budget that I vetoed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Not in an election year, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I told them in early ’95.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole said 30 years ago he was one of 12 people who voted against Medicare and he was proud of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A year ago he said, “I was right then.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I knew it wouldn’t work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: ” American seniors have the highest life expectancy in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to reform it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Not wreck it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, we’ve taken the first step.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Took it three steps, twice we sent welfare reform to the president and he vetoed it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: On the third time we sent welfare reform to the president he signed it but announced he would change it next year, and the vice president said they were going to do something else through the line item veto which I’ve never understood, but that’s sort of inside baseball.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: What we need to do is make certain we try to return people to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I’m standing here as someone who, a long time ago as the county attorney in Russell, Kansas, one of our jobs every month was go through all the welfare checks and sign them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And three of those checks were my grandparents’.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So I know what it’s like to have to look welfare head-on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Obviously some people are going to need help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You’re not going to go without food and you’re not going to go without medical care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But at the same time, if you want to get off Medicare, get back in the mainstream, we’re going to provide jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to say you have a five-year limit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You can be on welfare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You got two years to look for a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We provided more money for daycare in the bill that passed the senate, was vetoed, then it came back and the president signed pretty much the same bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But this is an important issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we ought to be giving welfare payments to illegal immigrants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It puts a heavy burden on a state like — except for emergencies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It puts a heavy burden on a states like California.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It costs California taxpayers 3 billion dollars a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Let me get out of your way here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s illegal right now and has been for years for illegal immigrants to get welfare benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say that this is one of the most important issues in the world to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I started working on welfare reform in 1980 because I was sick of seeing people trapped in a system that was increasingly isolating them and making their kids more vulnerable to get in trouble.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I’ve been working on it when I was a governor for a long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When I became president I used the authority I had in this law to get out from certain federal rules to help states move people to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We reduced the welfare rolls by 2 million already.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’ve got a plan with this new welfare reform law to work with the private sector, to give employees specific tax incentives to hire people off welfare, and to do some other things which will create more jobs in the private sector, at least a million, and move more people from welfare to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And I hope we get a chance to talk about this more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s not a more important issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I, I still remember a woman that I met ten years ago who said she wanted to get off welfare so her kids could tell, give an answer when they say, “What does your mother do for a job?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: ” I met that woman again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: She’s got four kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One’s got a good job, one’s studying to be a doctor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One’s in technical school, one’s an honor student in high school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to make more people like that woman, Lily Harden, so I’ve got a plan to do it, and it’s just beginning.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well another thing we can do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We talk about growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a great economic package which I hope we will discuss later.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Across-the-board tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Child credits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: $500 per child under 18.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Reduce the capital gains rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Create more jobs and opportunities for people on and off welfare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have other provisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Less litigation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The trial lawyers, big supporters of the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The trial lawyers, of course they like lawsuits, so every time they have a bill that they want vetoed, the president vetoes it for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to understand in America that we’ve got to have growth, create more jobs and more opportunities in the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The president takes credit for all these people off welfare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The governors did that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Federal government doesn’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And the government doesn’t create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They’re created in the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First of all, we have a big plan to reduce the capital gains tax when people sell their homes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Part of my tax package which is paid for in my balanced budget plan would exempt up to half a million dollars in gains from people when they sell their homes, which I think is the biggest capital gains benefit we could give to most ordinary Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We also have capital gains now for people that invest in new small businesses and hold the investment for five years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It was part of our other economic plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And these are things I think that will go a long way toward helping America build a stronger economy and a better tax system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I think the most important thing to emphasize, though, is that we also have to help people in other ways to build a strong economy and we can’t have any tax cut that’s not paid for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One of the big differences between Senator Dole and myself is that I told you how I’m going to pay for every penny of the tax cuts I recommend and we’ve worked hard to bring this deficit down and that’s helped people in the real estate business because the interest rates are lower.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got home ownership at a 15-year high.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got this country going in the right direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we can have a tax cut but my priority would be to help the families who need it with child rearing and education and buying a first-time home and helping for health care costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So from your business, helping in buying a first-time home, exempting the capital gains on the sale of the home would be the most important things that you asked about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Pamela.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Pam, what the president didn’t tell you is all his tax cuts expire the year 2000, but these increases go on forever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s the liberal approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know, give you a little tax cut, give you a couple of years, then make the tax increases go on forever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So the net tax increase in his plan’s somewhere between 60 and 80 billion dollars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We have in the Dole-Kemp economic plan, unless unless your home’s worth over 500,000 dollars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And if it is, I appreciate it congratulate you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But in any event, no tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a good idea, they saw it, they picked it up and put it in theirs, but it’s only temporary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Ours are permanent, ours is a good plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Create jobs and opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Capital gains rate, cut it in half, cut it 28 percent to 14 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are 7 trillion dollars in assets locked up in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If we cut the capital gains rate, I’m told everyday, I had a letter from a former constituent in Kansas saying I want to sell property in California, put it in my business in Kansas, I can’t, because the capital gains rate’s too high.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We need to get the economy going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’ll help social security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’ll create more jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’ll help people who want to get off welfare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s the American way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Before Senator Dole left the Senate, he and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Gingrich also were recommending that we pass these tax cuts only insofar as we could pay for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We all assume that the tax cuts will be permanent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But we have to prove we can pay for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: After he left the senate, we abandoned that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why most experts say that this tax scheme will blow a huge hole in the deficit, raise interest rates and weaken the economy and that will take away all the benefits of the tax cut with a weaker economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s why we have to balance the budget, and I will tell you how I’m going to pay for anything I promise you, line by line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You should expect that from both of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think age is very — you know, wisdom comes from age, experience and intelligence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And if you have some of each — and I have some age, some experience and some intelligence — that adds up to wisdom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think it also is a strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s an advantage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I have a lot of young people work in my office, work in my campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is about America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is about, somebody said earlier, one of the first questions, we’re together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s one America, one nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m looking at our economic plan because I’m concerned about the future for young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m looking about drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The president has been AWOL for four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m looking about crime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He’ll claim credit now for crime going down, but it happens because mayors and governors and others have brought crime down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Rudy Giuliani, Mayor of New York, brought crime down 25 percent just in New York City.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Of course the president will take credit for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: My view is we want to find jobs and opportunities and education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This year the Republican Congress, as far as student loans went from 24 billion to 36 billion over the next six years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: A 50 percent increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The highest appropriation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: 6 billion dollars for Pell Grants, very, very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We also raised the amount of each Pell Grant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In our economic plan, the $500 child credit can be used for young people, rolled over and over and over, you, of course not this age, but if you have a child two years old, 7 percent interest would be worth about $18,000 by the time that child was ready for college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I can only tell you that I don’t think Senator Dole is too old to be president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s the age of his ideas that I question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You’re almost not old enough to remember this.

transcript_turns.text: But we tried this before, promising people an election year tax cut that’s not paid for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You tried it last time you ran.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Tell him you can have everything you got.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And so let me just say this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Did you hear him say that Congress just voted to increase student loans and scholarships?

transcript_turns.text: They did after he left.

transcript_turns.text: The last budget he led cut Pell Grants, cut student loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I vetoed it when they shut the government down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My plan would give students a dollar-for-dollar reduction for the cost of a typical community college tuition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: A $10,000 deduction a year for the cost of college tuition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We let families save in an IRA, withdraw tax free to pay for the cost of education and it’s all paid for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My whole administration is about your future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s about what the 21st century is going to be like for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I hope you will look at the ideas in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When you don’t have any ideas, I guess you say the other person’s ideas are old.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: As I said earlier, they don’t have any ideas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Their ideas is to raise taxes and spend more money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s the liberal philosophy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s what you like, you’ve got a perfect candidate.

transcript_turns.text: President Clinton came to California in 1992.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He said the centerpiece in my first four years is going to be a middle class tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now all you got that tax cut, congratulations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Because you got a big tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You got a 265 billion dollar tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And he stands here and says politicians who make promises like that ought to be ignored.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well he made the promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I keep my word, and you will have a tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It will help you in whatever you’re going to do in the next few years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No, ma’am, I don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I am against quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m against giving anybody any kind of preference for something they’re not qualified for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But because I still believe that there is some discrimination and that not everybody has an opportunity to prove they’re qualified, I favor the right kind of Affirmative Action.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve done more to eliminate Affirmative Action programs I didn’t think were fair and tighten others up than my predecessors have, since affirmative action’s been around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I have also worked hard to give people a chance to prove that they are qualified.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me just give you some examples.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve doubled the number of loans from the small business administration, tripled the number of loans to women business people, no one unqualified, everybody had to meet the standards.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve opened 260,000 new jobs in the military to women since I’ve been president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But the joint chiefs say we’re stronger and more confident and solid than ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you another example of what I mean.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: To me, Affirmative Action is making that extra effort.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s sort of like what Senator Dole did when he sponsored the Americans with Disabilities Act and said to certain stores, okay, you have to make it accessible to people in wheelchairs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We weren’t guaranteeing anything, anybody anything except the chance to prove they were qualified, the chance to prove that they could do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why I must say I agree with General Colin Powell that we’re not there yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We ought to keep making those extra effort Affirmative Action programs, the law and the policy of the land.

transcript_turns.text: Well, we may not be there yet but we’re not going to get there by giving preferences and quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I supported that route for some time and again I think it gets back to experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: A little experience, a little age, a little intelligence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I noted that nobody was really benefitting except a very small group at the top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The average person wasn’t benefitting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: People who had the money were benefiting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: People who got all the jobs were benefiting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It seems to me that we ought to support the California civil rights initiative.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It ought to be not based on gender or ethnicity or color.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Or disability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m disabled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I shouldn’t have a preference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I would like to have one in this race, come to think of it, but I don’t get one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Maybe we can work that out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I get a 10-point spot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: No discrimination.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Discrimination ought to be punished but there ought to be equal opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to reach out, make certain everybody has a chance to participate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Equal opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But we cannot guarantee equal results in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s not how America became the greatest country on the face of the earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have never supported quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’ve always been against them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t favor equal results, but I do favor making sure everybody has a chance to prove they’re competent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The reason I have opposed that initiative is because I’m afraid it will end those extra effort programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Again I say, think of the Americans with Disabilities Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Make an effort to put a ramp up there so someone in a wheelchair can get up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You don’t guarantee they get the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You guarantee they have a chance to prove they’re competent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And as I said, this is not a partisan thing with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: General Colin Powell said the same thing, he fears the initiative would take away the extra effort programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: No preferences to unqualified people, no quotas, but don’t give up on making an extra effort until you’re sure everybody has a chance to prove they’re qualified.

transcript_turns.text: Well I’m glad you asked.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: What’s your first name?

transcript_turns.text: I first want to say the President didn’t quite give you all of the stuff on the quotas, because the Justice Department had what we called the Piscataway case up in New Jersey.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
