transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It shouldn’t be that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, the President can say well he wants to mend it, not end it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are 168 federal programs that allow quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He ended one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now, this economic package, Tim, I’m glad you asked, because you look like the type that might be able to benefit from a 15 percent across- the-board tax cut and $500-per-child tax credit, or — you know, estate tax relief which you’re not interested in right now, but capital gains rate reduction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If you’re taking care of an elderly parent, you get a $1,000 deduction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We think that’s very important because a lot of people take care of their parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: How do we pay for it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You can have a constitutional amendment to balance the budget, which the President opposed and defeated.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He twisted arms and got six Democrats to vote with him and lost by one vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to balance the budget, by the year 2002.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President wants to spend 20 percent more in the next six years, and I want to spend 14 percent more and give that 6 percent back to the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Remember, it’s your money; it’s not his money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And it’s not my money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s your money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And you shouldn’t have to apologize for wanting to keep all you can of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But he ought to apologize for wanting to take more and more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He wants to give you sort of a government tax cut, which really doesn’t mean anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You know, one of the responsibilities of growing older, it seems to me, is being able to tell people something they may not want to hear just because it’s true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: When they had a 250 billion dollar tax scheme, that is half the size of this one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This one is 550.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They passed the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: They have 270 billion dollars in Medicare cuts the first education cuts in history, cut environmental enforcement by 25 percent, took away the guarantee of quality standards in nursing homes, took away the guarantee of health care for folks with disabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Don’t take my word for this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The Economist magazine polled lots of economists, seven Nobel prize winners who said if this tax scheme passes, it will require huge cuts, 40 percent, in the environment and law enforcement and education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It will require bigger cuts in Medicare than I vetoed last time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: My targeted tax cut is for child-rearing, buying a first-time home, paying for health care costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And it’s paid for, and I’ll tell you how I’ll pay for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He won’t tell you because he can’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Your targeted tax cut, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President, never hits anybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s the problem with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Nobody ever gets it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I must say I’m a little offended by this word “scheme.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: ” You talked about it last time, you talked about a risky scheme and Vice President Gore repeated it about ten times in St.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Petersburg.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If I have anything in politics, it’s my word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: My colleagues, Democrats and Republicans, will tell you that Bob Dole kept his word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to keep my word to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to keep my word to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to tax — cut taxes and balance the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to touch Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to grow 39 percent, and Social Security is going to grow 34 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The President doesn’t have any ideas so he’s out trashing ours.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This isn’t going to blow a hole in the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He promised you a tax cut in 1992, and if you got one, you ought to vote for him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, well, first let me say that I signed the Family Leave Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It was my very first bill, and I’m very proud of it because it symbolizes what I think we ought to be doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I don’t take credit for all the good things that have happened in America, but I take credit for what I’ve tried to do to work with others to make good things happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Most important good things that happen in America happen in families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Just about every family I know, the main concern is how am I going to succeed at work and still do right by my children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Family medical leave has let 12 million families take a little time off for the birth of a child or a family illness without losing their job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to see it expanded in two ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to say you can also take a little time off without losing your job to go to a regular parent-teacher conference or to go to a regular doctor’s appointment with a family member.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’d also like to see the overtime laws change so that we could have some more flex time so that at the discretion of the worker, the worker, if you earn overtime, you could decide when you want that time to be taken, in cash or in time with your family if you’ve got a family problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I never go anywhere, it seems like, where I don’t meet somebody who has benefited from a Family Leave Law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: In Longview, Texas the other day, I met a woman who was almost in tears because she had been able to keep her job while spending time with her husband who had cancer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One of the people who’s here with me today met a woman in the airport saying her son, Jess was able to be present at the birth of her child because of the Family Leave Law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So yes, I think it should be expanded.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have to help people succeed at home and at work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, 88 percent of the people — the President claims 11 million are already covered and only 5 percent — keep in mind only 5 percent of the employers are affected by the Family Leave Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had a better idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t win.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had a better idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Now we have a majority and we get a president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That was a tax credit for the employer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Instead of the federal government, we had that tax credit, pick up some of the costs, because if you have to hire a replacement worker, that’s a cost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is the way it ought to work, give more power back to the states and back to the people back to the taxpayers, not always the long arm of the federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But keep in mind this bill covers 5 percent of the employers, and 95 percent of the employers and all those employees they employ are not covered in this act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And according to Investors Daily, which I read just a couple of days ago, 88 percent of the people he claims credit for are already covered in collective bargaining agreements or other agreements.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We had family leave in our office, I’m certain.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I see my friend Senator Mitchell.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: He had family leave.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I work every day with people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I spend a lot of time in hospitals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I know what it’s like to be in a hospital.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Sure we want family leave.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But there’s a better way to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I only have 30 seconds.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I can’t fix the statistics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It covers the majority of the work force.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Employers of under 50 are exempted.

transcript_turns.text: The bill originally covered employers of 25 and more, but because of opposition, we went up to 50.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Senator Dole led the opposition to it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He filibustered it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said it was a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He said it would hurt the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had record numbers of new small businesses and 10 and a half million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It didn’t hurt the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: He still believes it’s a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I believe it’s right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You can decide which of us you think are right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s up to you.

transcript_turns.text: Well, right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve lost 357,000 manufacturing jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics today said they made a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s probably going to take a much, much higher figure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So we talk about all these new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’d better wait and see what the results are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to do that with a more aggressive trade policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to do that with an economic package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now none of that will happen anymore.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I hope over the next ten years you will see a big increase over the percentage of people that have pension plans, plus a secure Social Security system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Did you say you’re unemployed?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: See, the first thing we have to do is get you a job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the economic package again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Create jobs and opportunities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Reduce the capital gains rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Reduce regulatory reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Stop some of this senseless litigation and let people work in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I think that’s that’s the thrust we will make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Obviously if Social Security is a very important program, it should — it will be preserved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Democrats or Republicans, it will be preserved.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We want to make certain we protect those in the pipeline just as we did back in 1983 and we did it on a bipartisan basis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We took it out of politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: people get so tired of politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to do the same with Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Maybe we can make a deal here tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you what we have done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have concluded with Japan 21 — about to be 22 — trade agreements now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And since we did that, in the areas where we concluded, trade agreements or exports to Japan have gone up by 85 percent in the last four years and our trade deficit with Japan has gone down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Until about five months ago the Japanese economy was in a deep recession.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s coming back now, so they can buy even more American products, and I think it will go down more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But I’m very — that’s one of the real success stories here of the work we’ve done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re selling Japanese rice from California for the first time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I visited a Chrysler dealership in Tokyo.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I visited a Jeep plant, oldest plant in America, a plant in Toledo, Ohio, where they’re going to export 41,000 right hand drive Jeeps this year, and they’ve got 700 new jobs because of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There’s no easy way to do this when you’re dealing with an economy that’s traditionally been more closed than one that’s traditionally been more open.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You have to gut it out, issue by issue by issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We agreed in principle on an insurance agreement, and we’re working on three or four other areas now, but the way you have to do it is make sure you’re competitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We’re the most competitive country in the world now, and then just fight to open those markets and go try to make the sale, and that’s what our trade ambassador our commerce secretary and all the other people in our administration are trying to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, the bottom line is we have to stop exporting jobs here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are 357, 000 good jobs — manufacturing jobs, which are lost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I assume some of those are because of our trading partners.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t have access to their markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to insist on access.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: If we don’t have access to their markets the same way they’ve access our markets, we ought to say, “Wait, that’s enough.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Time out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When you give us access, we’ll give you access.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: ” It’s very hard to get into the Japan market, as everybody knows.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They want to get into our market.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They sell a lot of automobiles here, create a lot of jobs — those who sell exports.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And that’s very important to the economy, but I think we want to make certain.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I supported the President’s trade policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But we got to be more aggressive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Once you have a policy, then you have to go out and be aggressive and enforce that policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are American jobs that are being lost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is what Ross Perot complains about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I’d say to the Reform party, take a look at the Republican party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re the reform party, and we’re going to make things better, and one of the things we’re going to do is stop exporting jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say again, we’ve had over 200 separate trade agreements in the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: By far, the largest number in American history — not just the big ones you read about, but a lot of smaller ones.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And now what we have to do is to focus on those things we’re real good at and make sure we’re getting a fair deal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We just had a pretty serious dispute with China because they were copying our CDs, and costing thousands of jobs in places like California.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we have — as we said, if you want to keep doing business and selling your products over here, you’re going to have to quit pirating our CDs, and they agreed to do things and verify that they had done it, which will make the problem much better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: There is not a simple answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You have to work on this day in and day out, every month ,every year, every issue, to make sure that we have not only free trade but fair trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud that we’re better off on that than we were four years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Hi, Rod.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well no doubt about it, our founding fathers had a great deal of wisdom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: In addition to what you mentioned, they also were concerned about this all-powerful central government in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: , that’d in effect confiscate your property, so — I carry it in my pocket — I can’t pull it out or I’d violate the rules — a copy of the Tenth Amendment which says we ought to return power to the states and the people, the people here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You ought to make more decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Honor, duty, and country, that’s what America is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Certainly the President of the United States, the highest office in the world, the most important office in the world, has a responsibility to young people, as we talked about earlier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: To everyone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: By example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to public ethics, he has a responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And you have 30-some in your administration, either left or being investigated or in jail or whatever, then you’ve got an ethical problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is public ethics; I’m not talking about private ethics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Talking about public ethics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: When you have 900 files gathered up by some guy who is a bouncer in a bar and hired a security officer to collect files, in Watergate — I know a person who went to jail for looking at one file, one FBI file.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are 900 sequestered in the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: People like you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Why should they be rifling through your files?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The president has a great responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: That’s one that I understand and certainly will carry out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is the most religious, great country in history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And yet, interestingly enough, we have the most religious freedom of any country in the world, including the freedom not to believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And now we have all these people just up the road in Los Angeles County, we have people from 150 different racial and ethnic groups and tons of different religions, but the fundamental tenets of virtually every religion are the same, and what I try to do is to support policies that would respect religion and then help parents inculcate those values to their children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me very briefly give you some examples.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One of my proudest moments was signing the Religious Freedom Restoration Act, that says the government has got to bend over backwards before we interfere with religious practice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So I changed the Justice Department’s effort to get a church to pay back a man tithe, because he was bankrupt when he gave it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I have supported character education programs in our schools, drug-free schools programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I supported giving parents a V-chip on their television so if they don’t want their young kids to watch things they shouldn’t watch, they wouldn’t have to.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That is the kind of thing we have to do, give people like you and our families the power to give those values to our children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s — before I came in, my wife and daughter and I had a prayer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Because it’s God’s will, whatever happens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s God’s will, it’ll happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: The constitutional amendment for voluntary prayer in school, in my view would be a great idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I support it; the president opposes it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It seems to me the president, whoever the president may be, this is one of his highest responsibilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: People look to the President of the United States more than any other person in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the way it’s always been, and that’s the way it always will be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to answer your question, but let me say one other thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We don’t need a constitutional amendment for kids to pray, and what I did was to have the justice department and the education department for the first time ever issue a set of guidelines that we gave to every school in America, saying that children could not be interfered with in religious advocacy when they were praying, when they were doing whatever they could do under the constitution, just because they were on a public school ground, and I think anyone who’s experienced this will tell you that our administration has done more than any in years to clarify the freedom of religion in the public square, including in the public schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think I have to let Senator Dole speak for himself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It wouldn’t be fair for me to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I would wind up — I mean, it’s the last question and I would mischaracterize it to try to make you happy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you what I feel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We have a lot of differences in our country, and some of us believe that other people’s decisions are wrong, even immoral.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: But under our constitution, if you show up tomorrow and obey the law, and you work hard and you do what you’re supposed to do, you are entitled to equal treatment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: That’s the way the system works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: All over the world, people are being torn apart — Bosnia, the Middle East, Northern Ireland, Rwanda, Burundi — you name it — because of all their differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We still have some of that hatred inside us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You see it in the church burnings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things I’ve tried hardest to do is to tell the American people that we have to get beyond that, we have to understand that we’re stronger when we unite around shared values instead of being divided by our differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, I hope I made my answer clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I said I’m opposed to discrimination.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: You know we’ve suffered discrimination in the disability community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are 43 million of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I can recall cases where people would cross the street rather than meet somebody in a wheelchair.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So we want to end discrimination.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I think that answers itself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: No discrimination in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’ve made that clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I would just say that it seems to me that that’s the way it ought to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We shouldn’t discriminate — race, color, whatever — life-style, disability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And we’re all proud of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But we’re not there yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: What we need is good, strong leadership going in the next century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry we didn’t have a foreign policy question, because just this week Secretary Christopher said, “Well, we really didn’t know much the first couple of years about foreign policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: ” Now that was quite an admission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It underscores what I had to say in the Hartford debate, that there is really no foreign policy in this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s sort of ad hoc, just whatever comes up, we’ll deal with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, we didn’t have more questions on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Let me say again, there is no more important responsibility for the president than to say if you believe in the constitution, the Bill of Rights, and the Declaration of Independence, that’s all we need to know.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And you can be part of our America and you can walk across that bridge to the 21st century with us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And we are not well served when we attack each other in a kind of ad hominem way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t educate children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It doesn’t solve problems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: We need to be disagreeing on ideas, honestly, and talking about the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The future will be the greatest time in this country’s history if we can beat this division that is bedeviling the whole rest of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me thank everybody here at the University and, Jim, thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: All the people who may still be watching or viewing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is what it’s all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s not about me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s not about President Clinton.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s about the process.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s about selecting a president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: So we have our differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We should have our differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Mentioned other parties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They have their differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We all agreed it would be a pretty dull place.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We should have more debates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Maybe we will have another debate on the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But I would just say this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: This is the highest honor that I have ever had in my life, to think that somebody from Russell, Kansas, somebody who grew up living in a basement apartment, someone whose parents didn’t finish high school, somebody who spent about 39 months in hospitals after World War II, someone who uses a buttonhook every day to get dressed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Somebody who understands that there’re real Americans out there with real problems, whether soccer moms, or the single parents, the families or the seniors, or people with disabilities, whoever it may be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: There are some very fundamental differences in this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President Clinton opposes term limits, President Clinton opposes a constitutional amendment to balance the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: President Clinton opposes voluntary prayer amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Opposes an amendment to protect the flag of the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: People give their lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Couple of service men here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: They sacrifice, they give everything for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We ought to protect the American flag with a constitutional amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: But beyond that we need to address the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I will just say my time is running out here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: It’s a very proud moment for me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: What I want the voters to do is to make a decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I want them to be proud of their vote in the years ahead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Proud that they voted for the right candidate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Proud that they voted hopefully for me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll just make you one promise, my word is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Democrats and Republicans said Bob Dole’s word is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I keep my word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: I promise you the economy is going to get better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have a good economic package.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: We’re going into the next century a better America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bob Dole
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And thank you, ladies and gentlemen, and all the people who are watching.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: One thing I would like to say is I agree with what Senator Dole said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: It’s a remarkable thing in a country like ours, a man who grew up in Russell, Kansas, and one who was born to a widowed mother in Hope, Arkansas, could wind up running for president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Could have a chance to serve as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: First thing I want to say is thank you for giving me the chance to be president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This election is about two different visions about how we should go into the 21st Century.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Would we be better off as I believe, working together to give each other the tools we need to make the most of our God-given potential, or are we better off saying, you’re on your own?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Would we be better off building that bridge to the future together so we can all walk across it or saying you can get across yourself?

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If you don’t agree — leave this room with anything else tonight and if the people watching us don’t leave with anything else, I hope you will leave with this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: This is a real important election.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: The world is changing dramatically in how we work and how we live, how we relate to each other, huge changes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: And the decisions we make will have enormous practical consequences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve talked about our responsibility tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: I want to talk about your responsibility, and your responsibility.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Your responsibility is to show up on November the 5th.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Because you’re going to decide whether we’re going to balance the budget now, but protect Medicare, Medicaid, education and the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: You will decide whether we’re going to keep fighting crime with a Brady Bill, assault weapons and finish putting those 100,000 police.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Whether we’re going to move a million people from welfare to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Whether we’re going to give our families more protection for their kids against drugs and tobacco and gangs and guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Whether we’re going to give our children a world-class education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Where every eight-year-old can read.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Every 12-year-old can log in on the Internet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Every 18-year-old can go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: If we do those things we will build that bridge to the 21st Century and the greatest country in history will be even greater.

transcript_turns.speaker: Bill Clinton
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.
